issues.legal_issue: Failure to seek rectification of an omitted issue under the former procedural law does not bar the issue from being raised in an appeal where that rectification procedure was procedural and had been repealed without a relevant accrued right.
material_facts: The defendants pleaded acquisition of title by prescription, and the issue was considered but left undecided by the lower appellate court.
The defendants did not seek rectification of the lower appellate court’s omission under the former procedural law.
The judgment containing the omission was delivered after the procedural provisions governing rectification had been repealed and superseded.
The defendants brought the matter to the Supreme Court by special leave.
issues.conclusion: The defendants were not barred from raising the plea of prescription in the appeal despite not having sought rectification of the lower appellate court’s omission.
issues.legal_principle: Under Articles 668, 669, 715, 722 and 677 of the Portuguese Civil Code, rectification of a judgment for an omission was a procedural step, not a vested substantive right of appeal. Under Section 4(1) of the Goa, Daman and Diu (Extension of the CPC and the Arbitration Act) Act, 1965, the former procedure was repealed, and the saving provisions did not preserve a rectification obligation or right that had not accrued before repeal. A right of appeal is generally substantive and preserved from the institution of the suit, subject to the exceptions stated in Garikapatti Veeraya v. N. Subbiah Choudhry and Colonial Sugar Refining Co. Ltd. v. Irving; the distinction between procedural and substantive provisions is also supported by Delhi Cloth and General Mills Co. Ltd. v. Income-tax Commissioner. The Court further relied on the plenary powers under Articles 136 and 142 of the Constitution, and Durga Shankar v. Raghuraj Singh, in holding that the appeal could not be barred by the former procedure.

rule.if: appeal_to_apex_court and lower_appellate_court_left_pleaded_issue_undecided and no_rectification_application_filed and rectification_procedure_was_procedural and no_relevant_right_or_obligation_accrued_before_repeal

predicates.appeal_to_apex_court: The matter is before the highest appellate court in an appeal.
predicates.lower_appellate_court_left_pleaded_issue: A lower appellate court did not decide an issue that a party had raised.
predicates.no_rectification_application_filed: The party did not apply to the lower court to rectify the omission.
predicates.rectification_procedure_was_procedural: The procedure for seeking rectification regulated how an undecided issue could be addressed and did not itself create a vested right of appeal.
predicates.no_relevant_right_or_obligation_accrued_: No right or obligation to seek rectification of the particular judgment had accrued before the former procedure was repealed.

issues.definition: When an appeal is before the highest appellate court, a party may raise an issue left undecided below despite not seeking rectification if the rectification procedure was procedural and no relevant right or obligation had accrued before its repeal.

issues.legal_issue: A trial court does not omit adjudication of an issue when it considers and rejects that issue, even if its reasoning is brief.
material_facts: The trial court framed a distinct issue concerning the defendants’ claim of long, public, peaceful and continuous possession.
The trial court discussed that claim and rejected it on the grounds that the possession originated under a lease and that the plaintiffs had also occupied the plot for a long period.
The trial court’s judgment was therefore not silent on the prescription issue.
issues.conclusion: The trial court had adjudicated the issue, so its judgment did not contain an omission requiring rectification under Article 669.
issues.legal_principle: Articles 668 and 669 of the Portuguese Civil Code treated abstaining from adjudication as a nullity that could be rectified by application. A brief decision rejecting an issue is not an abstention from adjudication and does not give rise to that nullity.

predicates.first_instance_civil_proceeding: The ruling concerns a civil case at the trial-court stage.
predicates.trial_court_considered_raised_issue: The trial court addressed an issue raised by a party.
predicates.trial_court_rejected_issue: The trial court gave a reason for rejecting the party’s position on that issue.

issues.definition: In a civil trial, consideration and rejection of a raised issue means the trial court adjudicated it rather than omitting it.

issues.legal_issue: A material issue raised in the pleadings and grounds of appeal should be remitted for a specific finding when the lower appellate court leaves it undecided.
material_facts: The defendants pleaded that they and their predecessors had possessed the property as owners for more than the required period and expressly relied on prescription.
The trial court framed an issue on the defendants’ possession and rejected the claim, while the defendants reiterated the prescription plea in their appeal.
The lower appellate court did not decide the prescription issue, which went to the root of the dispute.
The Supreme Court considered a finding from the lower appellate court necessary to do complete justice.
issues.conclusion: The Court remitted the case to the lower appellate court to rehear the parties and record a reasoned finding on whether the defendants had acquired title by prescription under the law applicable at the relevant time.
issues.legal_principle: The Supreme Court used its powers under Articles 136 and 142 of the Constitution to secure a finding on a pivotal issue left undecided below and to do complete justice. The Court remitted the issue for determination rather than deciding the merits of prescription itself.

rule.if: appeal_from_lower_appellate_decision and issue_pleaded_and_preserved_on_appeal and issue_material_to_dispute and lower_appellate_court_left_issue_undecided and finding_below_needed_for_complete_justice

predicates.appeal_from_lower_appellate_decision: The proceeding is an appeal from a decision of a lower appellate court.
predicates.issue_pleaded_and_preserved_on_appeal: A party raised the issue in the pleadings and maintained it in the appeal below.
predicates.issue_material_to_dispute: The issue could affect the outcome of the dispute.
predicates.lower_appellate_court_left_issue_undecid: The lower appellate court did not determine the issue.
predicates.finding_below_needed_for_complete_justic: The Supreme Court considered a reasoned finding by the lower appellate court necessary to resolve the appeal fairly.

issues.definition: When an appeal presents a material issue that was pleaded and maintained but left undecided below, the case is remitted if a lower-court finding is needed for complete justice.
